steps.title: Fat and protein
steps.body: Tannin binds to fat and protein, so Tannat shines with rich meat. In Uruguay, it's the wine of the asado, beef grilled slowly over wood. In Gascony, it goes with duck confit and cassoulet. The fat softens the tannin; the tannin cleans the palate.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve Tannat at 16 to 18 degrees. Young, powerful examples benefit from decanting for an hour or two. Good Madiran can age 10 to 20 years, when the tannins soften and earthy, leather notes emerge. Lighter Uruguayan styles are best within a few years.
steps.highlight: Decant young; good Madiran ages 10 to 20 years

steps.prompt: Which dish suits a young Tannat best?
steps.explanation: Fatty grilled meat softens Tannat's tannin. Delicate fish would taste metallic next to it.

steps.body: Uruguay's sweet fortified Tannat, sometimes called Tannat licoroso, is a good match for dark chocolate.

steps.prompt: Tannat is best served very cold, like a white wine.
steps.explanation: Not true. Cold makes tannin feel harsher. Serve it at 16 to 18 degrees.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Tannat loves fatty, grilled meat and duck
Serve at 16 to 18 degrees, and decant when young
Good Madiran ages for 10 to 20 years
